note: Every current `npm audit` advisory is dispositioned individually. No blanket/wildcard acceptance. Raw `npm audit` and `npm audit --omit=dev` output is always displayed and never suppressed; this register reviews findings, it does not hide them. Reconciled by tools/check-security-advisories.mjs (keyed by npmAuditId).

advisories.affectedFunction: Path traversal via previous source-map auto-loading (attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL in a CSS comment) → arbitrary .map file disclosure.
advisories.reachability: Not reachable: PostCSS runs only at build time over reviewed, repository-controlled CSS (Tailwind). No user/CMS/operator-authored/uploaded CSS, no runtime CSS-processing endpoint, no remote stylesheet piped through the build.
advisories.mitigation: Build input restricted to reviewed repo files + approved packages. Compliance test asserts no first-party module imports postcss and no approved route processes CSS.
advisories.compatibleStandardFixNote: npm's fix = next@9.3.3 (breaking downgrade). next 16.2.12 is latest stable and exact-pins postcss 8.4.31; direct transitive install is prohibited.
recheckTriggers: any untrusted input passed to PostCSS
a stable Next.js release bumping postcss

advisories.affectedFunction: Inherited libvips CVEs (CVE-2026-33327/33328/35590/35591) triggered when processing untrusted image input.
advisories.reachability: Not reachable: Next.js built-in image optimization is disabled globally (next.config.mjs images.unoptimized = true), so sharp/libvips never processes image bytes. No image upload, server-side transformation, or image-proxy endpoint; no untrusted image bytes; Google photos remain direct/live/unoptimized (existing compliance decision); no first-party import of sharp.
advisories.mitigation: images.unoptimized=true + compliance test asserting the flag, that no first-party code imports sharp, that no approved route does image transformation/proxying, and that Google media is not routed through the optimizer.
advisories.compatibleStandardFixNote: npm's fix = next@9.3.3 (breaking downgrade). next 16.2.12 allows only ^0.34.5 (excludes patched 0.35.x); direct transitive install is prohibited.
recheckTriggers: a stable Next.js release widening the sharp range

advisories.affectedFunction: esbuild development server allows any website to send requests to it and read responses (dev-server SSRF).
advisories.reachability: Not reachable under enforced architecture: drizzle-kit is used only as a local schema/migration-generation CLI. No esbuild serve, no Drizzle Kit studio, no migration tooling exposed as a service, no execution against untrusted project files; drizzle-kit is not shipped or executed in production.
advisories.mitigation: Governance check rejects esbuild-serve / drizzle-kit-studio scripts; drizzle-kit is a dev dependency and absent from the deployed runtime.
advisories.compatibleStandardFixNote: npm's fix = drizzle-kit@0.18.1 (breaking major downgrade). drizzle-kit 0.31.10 is latest stable and still bundles the legacy @esbuild-kit chain; fix needs upstream drizzle-kit to drop it.

advisories.affectedFunction: Code injection via _.template import key names.
advisories.reachability: Not reachable from untrusted input: the vulnerable lodash lives only inside the local Better Auth `auth` schema-generation CLI chain, which runs against the repository-controlled Better Auth config with no remote templates, user input, or provider payloads, and is never exposed as a service.
advisories.mitigation: `auth` is a dev dependency only and absent from the production bundle (compliance test); generation runs against reviewed repo config; generated output reviewed before migration generation; auth-generation smoke path preserved.
advisories.compatibleStandardFixNote: No patched lodash exists (4.17.21 is latest published; the advisory's fixed range >4.17.23 is unreleased). npm's fix = auth@1.2.3 (breaking major downgrade of the CLI).
recheckTriggers: auth CLI run in a shared service
auth moved to a production dependency
